title: Separation or overlap of whorls reflects the growth-rate ratio of outer to inner border

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Separation or overlap of whorls reflects the growth-rate ratio of outer to inner border

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Whether the whorls of a spiral shell stand apart, just touch, or overlap (up to complete involution, as in Nautilus pompilius versus N. umbilicatus) depends only on the ratio of the rate of growth of the outer border of the tube to that of its inner border.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For the purposes of the morphologist, then, the main result of this last general investigation is to shew that all the various types of “open” and “closed” spirals, all the various degrees of separation or overlap of the successive whorls, are simply the outward expression of a varying ratio in the _rate of growth_ of the outer as compared with the inner border of the tubular shell.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XI, “The Logarithmic Spiral”; topic “Contact and overlap of whorls”. Scope: discoid and turbinate molluscan shells, including nautiloids and ammonoids

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch11-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predicted association is quantitatively testable from existing scans. The word 'only' demands exclusion of correlated geometric factors, and inferred rates make that causal sufficiency less clean.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate outer- and inner-border growth increments from shell growth geometry and regress whorl separation, contact and overlap against their ratio. Test whether other parameters such as aperture shape and translation improve prediction beyond that ratio.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Several shell-model parameters can affect apparent overlap.

Static geometry only indirectly estimates growth rates.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open, touching and overlapping whorls are easy to score, and both nautiloid conditions are represented in public collections. A non-circular test needs the inner and outer rates from growth lines, which scans provide for a subset and ordinary photos often do not. Where only the outline is used, the result mostly restates the spiral geometry instead of discriminating a biological mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the outer-to-inner growth-rate ratio from growth increments independently of the adult outline, and predict whether whorls stand apart, touch or overlap, including the Nautilus pompilius versus N. umbilicatus contrast. A match supports the claim; overlap that disagrees with the increment ratio refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Many photographs do not resolve the increments needed for an independent rate.

Inside the logarithmic model, overlap is largely fixed by the expansion ratio, so an outline-only test is nearly geometric rather than empirical.
